promises.d: A 03:40 landing is a normal pickup time here, not a problem to solve at the desk. The name is the opening hours, not a slogan.
Nineteen cars, each one photographed and priced on its own page. You book that car, not a category with 'or similar' printed next to it.
Collect at arrivals, drop in town. Two locations, ten minutes apart, no fee for using both.
Eighteen of nineteen cars are automatic, which matters on Albanian mountain roads more than anywhere you have driven before.
One number, answered by someone in Tirana who can move a car. Not a queue, not a chatbot.

faq.a: Yes. Airport pickups run around the clock, seven days, including the night flights from Istanbul and Rome. Tell us the flight number and the car is there when you clear customs.
An EU, UK or US licence is accepted as it is. Licences in other alphabets should come with an International Driving Permit. Bring the physical card, a photo of it is not enough at the desk.

faq.q: Can I take the car to Kosovo, Montenegro or Greece?
faq.a: Cross-border travel is arranged case by case and needs the green card insurance document prepared in advance. Ask when you book, not on the day.

faq.q: Is the price per day the final price?
faq.a: The daily rate covers the car, basic insurance and unlimited kilometres inside Albania. Longer rentals are cheaper per day. Ask for the total before you commit and we will send it in writing.

The SH1 and SH2 are motorway standard. The coast road over Llogara and the routes into the mountains are narrow, steep and worth every minute. Take a diesel automatic and do not book the smallest car for the passes.

faq.q: Do you deliver the car to my hotel?
faq.a: Inside Tirana, yes, at no extra cost. Outside the city, ask and we will tell you honestly whether it is worth it.
You get the car full and return it full. The station nearest both offices is open all night, like we are.
Send the dates, the car and your flight number by WhatsApp or phone. You get a written confirmation the same day, usually within the hour.

roads.name: The Albanian Riviera
roads.carWhy: The one drive that earns a roof you can drop.
roads.story: The road climbs to a thousand metres at Llogara, turns a corner, and the whole Ionian coast is suddenly below you. Then it drops through Dhërmi and Himarë to water that has no business being that colour. This is the drive people fly here for.

roads.name: North to the Accursed Mountains
roads.best: June to September, closed in winter
roads.carWhy: The last hour to Theth is not a sedan road.
roads.story: The SH1 runs fast and flat to Shkodër, then the country stands up. The final climb into Theth is a mountain pass with a valley of stone houses at the end of it. Ground clearance is not optional on this one.

roads.name: Berat and Gjirokastër
roads.carWhy: Long, smooth kilometres. Take the comfortable boot.
roads.story: Two Ottoman towns, both UNESCO listed, both built as stacked stone windows on a hillside. Easy roads the whole way, which makes this the trip to hand to someone who is nervous about driving abroad.

destinations.name: Ksamil
destinations.carWhy: Long motorway run, take the comfortable one.
destinations.note: Three small islands close enough to swim to, in water that looks edited. Go in June or September: in August the road in is a car park and the beaches are full by nine.

destinations.name: The Blue Eye
destinations.carWhy: The last stretch is a rough track.
destinations.note: A spring nobody has found the bottom of, pushing cold water up through a pupil of dark blue. Park at the gate and walk the last kilometre. Swimming is officially discouraged and the water is about ten degrees anyway.

destinations.name: Butrint
destinations.note: Greek, Roman, Venetian and Ottoman ruins stacked in a forest on a lagoon, and a UNESCO site since 1992. Two unhurried hours. Go early, before the tour buses arrive from Corfu.

destinations.name: Gjirokastër
destinations.carWhy: Hills all the way, and cobbles at the end.
destinations.note: The stone city, built in slate and shuttered windows up a steep hillside under an enormous castle. The old town streets are cobbled and severe: park below and climb.

destinations.name: Lake Koman ferry
destinations.carWhy: Seven seats, and it takes the ferry with you.
destinations.note: A working ferry through a flooded canyon that people compare to the fjords and Halong Bay, and for once the comparison holds. The car goes on the boat. Book the crossing ahead in summer.

destinations.name: Valbona valley
destinations.hours: 5 h, or via the Koman ferry
destinations.carWhy: Gravel and river crossings. Ground clearance matters.
destinations.note: Alpine valley at the top of the country, and the start of the Valbona to Theth walk if you have a spare day. Snowed in through winter, so June to September only.

destinations.name: Krujë
destinations.carWhy: Half a day out. Take the cheapest key on the board.
destinations.note: Skanderbeg's castle above an Ottoman bazaar of carpets and copper. The easiest real day trip from Tirana, and the one to do on your first afternoon while you get used to the roads.

destinations.name: Shkodër and Rozafa
destinations.carWhy: Fast, flat motorway the whole way.
destinations.note: A castle on a ridge where three rivers and a lake meet, and the best sunset view in northern Albania. The city below is flat, green and full of bicycles.
